package_info.package_name: sniperv1 (and related: sniperv2, deuplouded, snipersee, sniperser)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages execute a Windows info-stealer and crypto-stealer ('Bladeroid') immediately upon installation, exfiltrating browser cookies, local storage, autofill data, crypto wallet data, and session tokens for various services to an attacker-controlled domain. The packages use obfuscated/encrypted payloads, misleading documentation, and postinstall scripts to evade detection and maximize data theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the postinstall script executes index.js, which initiates the malware execution chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running arbitrary code at install time is a common malware tactic, especially when not required for legitimate package functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require postinstall scripts unless performing necessary setup; here, it is used solely to launch malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall for compiling native modules or setup, but not for launching info-stealers.
key_indicators: postinstall script with no legitimate purpose
triggers execution of further malicious code

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, index.js loads and executes gayy.js, which contains the encrypted payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code misleads by referencing a non-existent file (sa.js) and instead loads an obfuscated payload, a common evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not mislead about which files are executed or load encrypted payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, obfuscation is used for intellectual property protection, but not for postinstall scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, gayy.js decrypts a large encrypted payload and executes it in memory, launching the main stealer logic.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Decryption and in-memory execution of a large, hidden payload is a hallmark of malware seeking to evade static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not decrypt and eval large hidden payloads during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may decrypt configuration or license data, but not full executable payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the decrypted payload scans known filesystem paths for browser cookies, local storage, Discord, Telegram, FileZilla, and crypto wallet data, reads and processes these files, and prepares them for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and reading sensitive application data from multiple unrelated programs is a clear sign of info-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not access or exfiltrate browser, wallet, or session data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities may access user data, but only with explicit user consent and not during package installation.
key_indicators: hardcoded paths to sensitive app data
broad targeting of multiple unrelated applications

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates browser extension directories for known crypto wallet extensions (MetaMask, BinanceChain, etc.), reads their data, and exfiltrates it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Targeting crypto wallet extensions for data theft is a high-value attack vector and not a legitimate package behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not access or exfiltrate browser extension data, especially for wallets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for this behavior in a general npm package.
key_indicators: filesystem access to browser extension data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code locates and reads session data for social media and streaming services (Instagram, Reddit, TikTok, Spotify), then exfiltrates the session tokens.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting session tokens for unrelated services is a clear sign of credential/session theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or exfiltrate session data for third-party services.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for this behavior.
key_indicators: targeting of multiple social media/streaming session data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends all harvested sensitive data to an attacker-controlled webhook at bladeroid.xyz via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive data to an external domain is the defining behavior of info-stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not send user data to external servers without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting may send limited, anonymized data, but not sensitive credentials or wallet data.

attack_chain.action: Postinstall script in package.json executes index.js upon installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: index.js loads and executes the next stage payload.

attack_chain.action: index.js loads gayy.js, which contains the encrypted payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: gayy.js decrypts and executes the main stealer payload.

attack_chain.action: gayy.js decrypts and evals the main stealer code in memory.
Main payload scans filesystem for browser, Discord, Telegram, FileZilla, and crypto wallet data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is collected for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Main payload locates and reads session tokens for Instagram, Reddit, TikTok, Spotify.
attack_chain.leads_to: Session tokens are collected for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: All harvested data is exfiltrated to bladeroid.xyz via HTTPS POST.

behavioral_signatures: npm package with postinstall script executing index.js or similar
Execution of obfuscated/encrypted payloads with in-memory decryption and eval
Filesystem access to browser, Discord, Telegram, FileZilla, and crypto wallet data paths
Network exfiltration to hardcoded domains (e.g., bladeroid.xyz)
Harvesting and exfiltration of session tokens for social media and streaming services
file_indicators: index.js that loads a misleading or non-existent file
gayy.js or similarly named file containing encrypted payload
References to browser/crypto wallet/Discord/Telegram/FileZilla data paths
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to bladeroid.xyz or related domains
Unusual outbound connections immediately after npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute JavaScript files. Flag packages that decrypt and eval large payloads at install time. Detect access to sensitive application data paths (browsers, wallets, Discord, Telegram, FileZilla) by NodeJS processes during or immediately after installation. Alert on outbound network connections to known malicious domains (e.g., bladeroid.xyz) or bulk exfiltration of local data. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify obfuscated payloads and hardcoded exfiltration endpoints.
